15 Computational health informatics using evolutionary-based feature selection

Vanaja Ramaswamy
Department of Information Science and Technology, College of Engineering Guindy, Anna University, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India
Saswati Mukherjee
Department of Information Science and Technology, College of Engineering Guindy, Anna University, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India

Abstract

This chapter is a recent survey of evolutionary computation (EC)-based feature selection (FS) techniques whose objective is mainly to improve the accuracy of the machine learning algorithm in minimized computation time. The idea is to bring forth the main strengths of EC as a naturally inspired optimization technique for FS in the machine learning process. The modeling of biological and natural intelligence that has made progressive advancements in the recent decade motivates us to review state-of-the-art FS techniques to add more to the area of computational intelligence. Owing to its importance, the use-case in support of health informatics is also exhibited.

Keywords: Evolutionary Computation, Feature selection, Machine learning, Computational intelligence,

15.1 Introduction

The chapter introduces machine learning techniques with a focus on feature selection (FS) and reviews the recent state-of-the-art FS mechanisms and their types. FS as an essential sub-process in machine learning allows the learning algorithm to train faster and improves the accuracy of the model by choosing the right subset of features (Dash and Liu, 1997). It also results in a better understanding of the data with good generalization capability. The predictive performance is highly improved when a machine learning task is preceded by an effective FS approach. The chapter explains the general notion of filter-based method and wrapper-based method of FS with the differences in their respective approaches. A general FS (filter/wrapper) is readily applicable as long as the number of features available in the data set is small. As we progress to access big data, both in terms of the sample size and the feature size, no more general approach can do well as the search space is very large (Xue et al., 2015). The immediate need is a mechanism that randomly starts with a heuristic and proceeds on with effective moves in the search of the global optimal position. Therefore, the interest of the chapter is to provide an overview of the evolutionary paradigm of FS mechanism and their importance in computational intelligence. Due to its global exploration ability in search, the evolutionary approach of FS namely genetic algorithm (GA), genetic programming (GP), particle swarm optimization (PSO), ant colony optimization (ACO), and others have become popular in the recent past of the research (De La Iglesia, 2013). This chapter categorizes the FS as filter-based evolutionary methods (FBEM), wrapper-based evolutionary methods (WBEM), and hybrid-based evolutionary methods (HBEM). It explains these three categories of FS with a specific combination of the above-mentioned evolutionary approaches based on the relevance of application and the need for implementation. Concerning the time-sensitiveness of the industry, healthcare is considered as an application where specific use-cases one for FBEM and the other for WBEM are discussed.

15.2 Machine learning techniques with a focus on feature selection

“Machine learning is a kind of artificial intelligence which provides an automated learning ability for a system by using the experiences gained in the past.” As irrelevant and redundant features can impact the performance of a model negatively (https://towardsdatascience.com/feature-selection-techniques-in-machine-learning-with-python-f24e7da3f36e), they can be removed before the learning phase of a machine learning cycle.

FS as an efficient pre-processor can be added as an important paradigm to do this to bring improvement both in time and space complexity.

15.2.1 Terminologies involved with machine learning

The following are the terminologies involved for machine learning paradigm:

  • Model

    A model is a hypothetical representation that learns some concepts from the data by using machine learning techniques.

  • Dataset

    The file that contains “n” number of instances (records to be trained) represented in rows and “f” number of features represented as columns.

  • Feature Vector and features

    The individual record of a data set will constitute a feature vector and each entity in the feature vector represents a feature.

  • Target (Label)

    An output label that a record is associated with is called the target. This will apply to supervised learning methods.

  • Training

    A machine learning algorithm is used to generate patterns that result out of the learning model.

  • Prediction

    New data can be applied to the model to make a prediction based on the features of the data.

In any machine learning technique, FS mechanism plays an important role to provide the model, good generalization ability, shorter training time, and increased accuracy and also helps in simplifying the model for the better interpretation for users (Cai et al., 2018).

As shown in Figure 15.1, the pre-processing of raw data is performed to make the data ready for the FS process. This is followed by the learning phase that uses some effective machine learning algorithms. When there are several machine learning approaches like supervised learning, unsupervised learning, semi-supervised learning, and reinforcement learning, the diagram mainly explains the supervised learning mechanism where the data with its target is used. The evaluation process to measure accuracy and other required metrics can be performed on the test data set. Now the developed and tested model is ready for making new predictions.

15.3 General types of feature selection and their differences

FS techniques are in general classified as filter, wrapper, and embedded methods (Chandrashekar and Sahin, 2014).

15.3.1 Filter-based FS methods

The filter-based FS approach applies some statistical methods like information gain, correlation coefficient, or others to assign a numeric score to each feature based on which feature ranking will be performed. This feature ranking can be used either to use the features or not, based on the requirement of the application.

As shown in Figure 15.2, the selection of features is independent of any machine learning algorithm (https://www.analyticsvidhya.com/blog/2016/12/introduction-to-feature-selection-methods-with-an-example-or-how-to-select-the-right-variables/).

15.3.2 Wrapper-based FS Methods

In the wrapper-based FS method, a feature subset is generated and is given as input to a learning model. Based on the output of the previous model, features can be added or removed; or a new feature subset can be formed based on some evaluation criteria. The problem is essentially reduced to a search problem. The flow of the method is shown in Figure 15.3.

15.3.3 Hybrid and embedded FS methods

The hybrid method is a mixture of filter and wrapper methods. Algorithms in embedded methods have an in-built FS mechanism. The most common examples are Lasso and Ridge regression techniques where they perform L1 and L2 regularization, respectively, to reduce overfitting.

15.3.4 Difference between filter-based and wrapper-based FS methods

While it is possible to use hybrid method that combines the characteristics of filter and wrapper, yet there are internal differences between filter-based and wrapper-based FS.

Such differences are mentioned in Table 15.1 concerning some specific characteristics.

Table 15.1:Difference between filter and wrapper FS method.

S.No. Characteristics Filter-based FS method Wrapper-based FS method
1. Methodology They measure the relevance of features by using their correlation with the dependent variable They measure the usefulness of a subset of features by training a model on it.
2. Speed Faster (as they do not involve training the model) Comparatively slow
3. Computational cost Computationally inexpensive Computationally expensive
4. Evaluation methods used Statistical methods Cross-validation techniques
5. Accuracy Inaccurate (Fails to find the best subset of features) Accurate (Provides the best subset of features)

15.4 An overview of evolutionary paradigm for feature selection

The diagram in Figure 15.4 represents the taxonomy that classifies the evolutionary methods of FS as filter-based, wrapper-based, and hybrid-based. All the above-mentioned types of evolutionary methods can be classified based on the techniques followed such as evolutionary algorithm or swarm intelligence. The categories mentioned under each type like GA, GP under EA, and PSO, ACO under swarm intelligence are the basic interest of the chapter based on the recent research progresses in these areas.

The upcoming sections explain some of the recent state-of-the-art research with the following combinations as mentioned below,

  • Filter-based GA (FB-GA), filter-based GP (FB-GP), filter-based PSO (FB-PSO), and filter-based ACO (FB-ACO).

  • Wrapper-based GA (WB-GA), wrapper-based GP (WB-GP), wrapper-based PSO (WB-PSO), and wrapper-based ACO (WB-ACO).

  • Hybrid-based GA (HB-GA), hybrid-based GP (HB-GP), hybrid-based PSO (HB-PSO), and hybrid-based ACO (HB-ACO).

15.5 Filter-based evolutionary methods of feature selection

The following subsections explain the recent research progresses in filter-based mechanism executed in combination with GA, GP, PSO, and ACO evolutionary approaches.

15.5.1 FB-GA

The initialization and the operations in the evolutionary approach of genetic algorithms are modified by introducing the concept of grouping the individuals as tribes. It is ensured that the features selected in each tribe follow Gaussian distribution. The exploration ability of individual tribes is compared to determine the competing tribes that are allowed to produce more individuals to search their respective solution space effectively. The proposed algorithm is compared with many existing FS approaches and is experimentally determined to produce accurate pattern classification (Ma and Xia, 2017). FS that provides maximum discriminating ability using a fine level of information is proposed. A binary genetic algorithm is used with rough set concept for the above-mentioned feature granulation (Dong et al., 2018).

15.5.2 FB-GP

The genetic programming approach based on parsimony pressure is used for figure-ground segmentation as a preprocessing step in the image processing task. The experimental results of the proposed work are compared with many existing FS mechanisms and have shown improvement in F1-score (Liang et al., 2016). A new FS method is proposed to perform symbolic regression for high-dimensional data. The main objective of the system is to show improvement in the generalization ability using the regression task (Chen et al., 2017). Automatic FS using image descriptor is proposed. GP has been utilized to synthesize a descriptor. Experiments have been conducted for classifying the image texture with different rotational degrees and compared with domain expert knowledge to assess the proposed system effectiveness (Al-Sahaf et al., 2016).

15.5.3 FB-PSO

A filter-based FS with a variant of PSO embedded with the GA is proposed to mitigate the premature convergence problem that exists in the conventional PSO approach. The work uses non-replaceable memory, secondary swarm, and a new update mechanism in velocity. In-depth analysis is performed for recognizing seven facial emotions by using multiple classifiers (Mistry et al., 2016). When exhaustive search does not result in the effective selection of features due to time-consumption, the use of a meta-heuristic PSO algorithm serves good in efficient search of the solution space. The proposed work has performed filter-based FS where the performance of the classifier and the selected features length are adopted as heuristic information. The experiments are conducted on benchmark data sets (Aghdam and Heidari, 2015).

15.5.4 FB-ACO

Novel selection of features is performed using a combination of graph clustering and ACO. One of the algorithms for detecting the communities is used after performing clustering and as a third step, ACO is used as a search paradigm to select the final subset of features. The evaluation is performed using the separability index and executed as a filter-based approach (Moradi and Rostami, 2015). A modified version of binary-coded ACO is combined with GA to perform filter-based FS. The proposed works have modeled on two aspects, one based on visibility density and the other based on pheromone density. The performance is analyzed by comparing the other existing and leading methods based on GA and PSO, and it is found that the proposed approach is better in terms of accuracy (Wan et al., 2016).

15.6 Wrapper-based evolutionary methods

The following subsections explain the recent research progresses in wrapper-based mechanism executed in combination with GA, GP, PSO, and ACO evolutionary approaches.

15.6.1 WB-GA

A bi-objective genetic algorithm is used for selecting the features where rough set and information theories are used for the definition of the objective function. A parallel implementation of ensemble FS is performed to reduce the execution time by using the pareto-based approach (Das et al., 2017). Credit scoring in financial computation is handled using two methods namely information gain-based and wrapper-based genetic algorithm where for assessing the features K-nearest neighbor, Naive Bayes, and support vector machine classifiers are used. The observation from the results implies that classification accuracy mostly depends on the nature of the dataset used (Jadhav et al., 2018). To differentiate between normal and abnormal traffic, an anomaly-oriented intrusion detection system is proposed using the genetic algorithm and support vector machine. The new form of FS that uses the genetic algorithm makes a difference in terms of the fitness function used. More stable features are selected which have effectively reduced the false positive rate (Gharaee and Hosseinvand, 2016). The work proposes a multi-stage FS mechanism to select the best parameters based on the time-frequency domain. GA is used in a supervised environment for selecting the best features along with the artificial neural network as a classifier. The exploration and exploitation abilities of the genetic algorithms are studied in the experiment conducted. The whole of the work is dedicated to condition-based monitoring of gearboxes (Cerrada et al., 2015).

15.6.2 WB-GP

GP is used for powerful FS to improve the performance of segmentation in the standard classification process. The work has proposed three FS techniques that are tested using standard classifiers and are executed on two high varying datasets. Investigations of single and multiple objectives GP techniques have been performed (Liang et al., 2017). An ensemble way of genetic programming is proposed for effective FS where the c-class problem is divided into c binary classification problem. A weighted voting scheme has been adopted in the ensemble that uses false-positive and false-negative values on the training data. The work is compared with a bi-objective GP scheme that uses a reduction of rule size strategy and the proposed method holds good (Nag and Pal, 2015).

15.6.3 WB-PSO

A new wrapper-based FS is proposed to improve the capability of a classifier to classify datasets which are incomplete. PSO is used for searching the feature subsets and C4.5 is used as the classifier to assess the feature subsets. Empirical results are obtained and analyzed on 14 datasets (Tran C.T. et al., 2016). A variant of PSO named as competitive swarm optimizer is used for resolving FS for high-dimensional problems. Here, the developed algorithm is used as a combinatorial optimization technique rather than being used as a continuous optimization technique. To reduce the cost of computation, an archive technique is also developed (Gu et al., 2018). PSO-based FS is performed with local search combined with gbest resetting mechanism to find the solution for local optima problem. The proposed algorithm is compared with three existing FS techniques. To ensure good generalization ability, it is noticed from the developed system that bias in FS should be avoided (Tran et al., 2016). For effective retrieval and analysis of an image, the semantic concepts should be assigned to an input image. An improved quantum-based PSO for selecting the features and ensemble-based boosting technique has been used in the research (Jin and Jin, 2015).

15.6.4 WB-ACO

The proposed work selects the optimal features without the use of prior information using ACO for searching and one classifier for assessing the features selected. The development of a facial recognition system is the application proposed in the work (Dadaneh et al., 2016). Wrapper-based approach in selecting the features is executed for the application of intrusion detection. The work uses support vector machine for validating the reduced data set. On performing the experiments on KDD99 dataset, the detection based on signature and anomaly is intended to be performed (Mehmod and Rais, 2016).

15.7 Hybrid-based evolutionary methods

The following subsections explain the recent research progresses in hybrid based mechanism executed in combination with GA, GP, PSO- and ACO evolutionary approaches.

15.7.1 HB-GA

To show improvement in randomization and search operation, the genetic algorithm is enhanced with new crossover and mutation operations. The comparison between the GA and the proposed enhanced GA results in a reduction in dimensions and time. Accurate categorization of text is performed by bringing forth some hybrid FS methods along with the enhanced genetic algorithm concept (Ghareb et al., 2016). Owing to several limitations that exist in the existing FS techniques, a hybrid GA that combines wrapper and embedded FS methods is proposed. A novel chromosome encoding is used where the objective is to optimize the control parameters for good optimization (Liu et al., 2018). A hybrid GA for efficient local search is proposed that works in combination with K-nearest neighbor classifier. The features are ranked and associated weight is given to those features during the classification process. The system is proposed to be applied for bringing innovation in management during the strategic decision making process (Eroglu and Kilic, 2017).

15.7.2 HB-GP

High-dimensional feature construction and selection is executed to produce smaller feature sets that will improve the performance of the learning algorithm. A hybrid approach is followed and is applied to six high-dimensional data sets to prove the efficiency of the proposed work. Dynamically tuned evolutionary GP approaches have boosted the performance of the system (Tran et al., 2016, December).

15.7.3 HB-PSO

Correlation information-based local search strategy is used with the existing PSO concept to guide the search process effectively. The proposed work also determines the size of the feature subset to select the subset with a reduced size. The comparison with the existing state-of-the-art filter-based FS methods has been performed to show the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid strategy (Moradi and Gholampour, 2016). A hybrid FS strategy is first proposed where most of the evaluations in the search process of PSO are filter-based and some of the evaluations are wrapper-based. The second proposal includes reducing the number of evaluations for wrapper-approach in order to save time. The proposed work depicts that the wrapper-approach results in achieving high classification performance with a reasonable number of selected features and the filter-approach results in good accuracy with a reduced number of features during the selection process (Butler-Yeoman et al., 2015).

15.7.4 HB-ACO

ACO is used both for FS and classification by using the Ant-Miner classifier. The proposed hybrid method of FS performs well in comparison with other existing methods to discriminate the input features properly and in the optimal way of selecting the features (Rasmy et al., 2012). An ensemble classifier is coupled with ACO algorithm to perform effective FS and to improve the predictive accuracy of filters. Experiments are conducted on 11 publicly available data sets operated over four different classifiers. The results show that the proposed hybrid approach outperforms many existing FS techniques (Naseer et al., 2018).

15.8 Medical and other general surveys on feature selection (includes GA, GP, PSO, and ACO)

To detect arrhythmia in heart patients using ECG signals, a novel three-layer genetic algorithm-based classifier is built. The developed method combines the advantages of ensemble learning, deep learning, and evolutionary computation (EC). The experiments conducted by using the developed method have shown good classifier accuracy along with better recognition sensitivity in detecting the disease (Pławiak and Acharya, 2019). The parallel processes of FS along with parameter optimization of the artificial neural network have been designed using the GA for automatic diagnosis of breast cancer in women. The proposed method uses three types of back-propagation techniques for the effective diagnosis of the disease. The resilient back-propagation approaches of the proposed algorithm have produced the best results experimentally (Ahmad F and Isa, 2015). Mutation operation is applied aggressively in the GA to perform FS to design the brain–computer interface (BCI). The proposed FS is compared with the existing FS techniques that apply to BCI and the method is found to be superior (Rejer, 2015). A multi-objective system is proposed for intrusion detection where the problem of imbalanced classification is handled effectively. Method of special domination and predefined search based on multiple targets are the two strategies used. The work consists of bias-selection and fit-selection processes to handle the imbalanced data set to perform efficient FS (Zhu et al., 2017). A rough set theory based FS is performed using a group incremental approach where the genetic algorithm is used for selecting optimal features. The objective is to perform FS dynamically by using the reduct set that is obtained in the previous generation in the optimization process (Das et al., 2018). A tree-based embedded approach can be used for feature construction and selecting the features implicitly. The proposed work is used for high-dimensional data classification. Experimental investigations have been performed on seven high-dimensional gene expression problems and analyses of overfitting occurrence also have been handled (Tran et al., 2016, March). In the gene selection process to identify cancer, k-means clustering is used for redundancy removal and random forest is used for ranking the genes inside every cluster. The filtered genes are used in the classification process where eight benchmark classification methods are used. The filtered genes are also given as input to PSO + boosted C5.0 to compare the performance of the combined approach with eight benchmark classified output (Pashaei et al., 2015). FS, which is an NP-hard problem, is performed on liver and kidney datasets to be used in the intelligent diagnosis system of diseases. Two modified PSO algorithms named velocity bounded and improved velocity bounded PSO algorithms are proposed to be used in the diagnosis system. The results of the new two algorithms are compared with the existing Boolean PSO algorithm and found to be comparatively better in selecting the features for the mentioned data sets (Gunasundari et al., 2016). To help pathologists in the diagnosis of breast cancer, the proposed system performs bandwidth selection and other feature subset selection for the estimation of kernel density in the decision making process. The work combines PSO with a kernel density estimator based classifier to perform the diagnosis. The objective function designed is used to show improvement in classification performance and the number of features selected (Sheikhpour et al., 2016). Ant activities have shown its importance in resolving several problems based on combinatorial optimization. Several filter-based iterations help in finding the optimal subset of features. To remove redundancy, feature relevance is used to find feature similarity. The output of FS is evaluated using the SVM classifier and the accuracy comparison between the whole set of features and selected features are performed (Sabeena and Sarojini, 2015). The search capability is improved using the probability method of encoding, hybrid operator and domination in Pareto relationship. The proposed cost-based multi-objective approach of FS is compared with other multi-objective algorithms for FS. The experiments are conducted on five benchmark datasets (Zhang et al., 2017).

15.9 Application of filter-based and wrapper-based PSO for health care informatics

15.9.1 Filter-based feature selection using a variant of PSO with digital pheromone concept

As the basic PSO method usually suffers from the local optima problem, the proposed variant of PSO uses digital pheromone as a third important component in the velocity update. This proposed methodology is executed as a filter-based model for the FS process (Ramaswamy and Mukherjee, 2019). The decrease in the computation time and increase in the classifier accuracy of the proposed FFS-PSODP have motivated to conduct the experimental results on four benchmark datasets taken from the UCI machine learning repository (https://archive.ics.uci.edu/ml/datasets.php). New fitness functions were designed for handling imbalanced datasets. The performance analysis for diabetes disease in balanced data set and hepatitis disease in imbalanced data set are handled in the proposed work and shared as obtained below. The existing filter-based FS techniques that are considered for comparison are pair-wise correlation, Eigen-centrality, relief, and PSO. The proposed work has used the FFS-PSODP algorithm and has performed comparatively better in achieving good accuracy in possible minimum time.

The graph in Figure 15.5 shows the performance comparison of the existing FS techniques with the proposed algorithm for balanced data set of diabetes disease.

The graph in Figure 15.6 shows the performance comparison for imbalanced data set of hepatitis disease.

15.9.2 Wrapper-based feature selection using a variant of PSO with digital pheromone concept

The wrapper-based approach has implemented two FS mechanisms that use a variant of PSO with digital pheromone concept. Feed-forward neural network, back-propagation neural network and recurrent neural network are used in the classification process. The proposed novel approaches have given closely accurate results in minimum time (Vanaja and Mukherjee, 2018). The performance comparison uses the existing FS techniques like pair-wise correlation, Eigen-centrality, latent, relief, and PSO where they have been used as a wrapper and compared with the proposed PSODP and PSO + PSODP techniques. The graphs in Figures 15.7 and 15.8 that uses the proposed two novel approaches have shown that for both breast cancer and chronic kidney disease data sets, they have performed comparatively better than the existing approaches.

The performance is evaluated and shows the achievement of the two proposed methods in getting good accuracy in minimum time constraint.

15.10 Acknowledgement

The first author would like to thank the “Visvesvaraya PhD Scheme,” MeitY, New Delhi to support and appreciate the efforts financially in the form of scholarship.

15.11 Conclusion and future work

The chapter has contributed to reviewing some of the recent state-of-the-art research works in evolutionary approaches of FS. It is analyzed that in the past 5 years, there are reasonable FS approaches used with ACO and GP techniques. It is also noticed that there is number of research contributions for FS mechanism that have been used with GA and PSO. Owing to the importance of FS tasks in the machine learning cycle, it is believed that the research progression using evolutionary approaches of the search paradigm will be exponential in the mere future arena of computational intelligence. In particular, the contributions made in the health informatics domain have taken more importance when compared to other industries or applications. Thus, the interest of the chapter proposal has extended in explaining the implementation results that have been obtained through filter and wrapper approaches of FS using a variant of PSO to build an efficient clinical decision support system. As future plan, there are extended ideas to survey all the possible evolutionary approaches used for the FS process with regard to different time sensitive and time insensitive applications.
